title: Banana Chickpea Muffins
description: Moist, wholesome, and protein-packed—these banana chickpea muffins are a deliciously healthy twist on a classic favourite.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "183 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "26 g", "proteinContent": "6 g", "fatContent": "7 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "84 mg", "fiberContent": "4 g", "sugarContent": "7 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "5 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 2 cups (18 ounce) can chickpeas drained + rinsed
½ cup tahini or almond butter
1.5 cups rolled oats gluten-free if preferred
banana slices, chocolate chips, blueberries, nuts
steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and use a greased muffin tin or line a muffin pan with muffin liners.
Mash your banana to ensure you have 1 cup worth of mashed banana. Then add all the ingredients except for any optional toppings to your food processor. Process the mixture until mostly smooth.
Divide the batter between your 12 muffin cups and top some or all of the muffins with toppings if you'd like.

Bake the chickpea muffins for 20-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the middle of a muffin comes out mostly clean. Then remove them from the oven and let them cool for 10-15 minutes before transferring them to a cooling rack.
hints: Use overripe bananas. The riper your bananas, the greater flavour, sweetness, and moisture they will add to your banana chickpea muffins. Bananas with brown skin work best.
Use baking powder that is fresh and ACTIVE . Baking powder that is open in the pantry for 6+ months may lose its effectiveness.
Measure your mashed banana to ensure you're using one cup. Bananas vary greatly in size. Two large bananas or three medium bananas work for me.
Let your muffins cool for 10-15 minutes before removing them from the muffin pan to help them set and prevent them from breaking.
Leftover muffins will keep at room temperature for 1-2 days, refrigerated for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Chickpea Fajitas
description: Spice up your dinner with these easy sheet pan chickpea fajitas!

ingredients: 3 bell peppers (sliced (I used 1 red, 1 green, 1 orange))

Slice and arrange your veggies and the chickpeas in a single layer on your baking sheet.
Combine all the marinade ingredients in a small bowl. Then evenly drizzle it over the chickpeas and vegetables.
Bake the veggies for 10-12 minutes. Then optionally, broil them for another 1-3 minutes to brown the veggies.
Serve with corn tortillas and any additional toppings you'd like.

title: Potato Asparagus Salad
description: This vibrant potato asparagus salad is a perfect celebration of spring flavours!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "182 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "37 g", "proteinContent": "7 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "23 mg", "fiberContent": "7 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 2 pounds mini potatoes scrubbed clean (I used a mix of red and yellow)
1 pound asparagus ends trimmed + cut into 1-inch pieces
¼ cup fresh chives finely chopped
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the peas and asparagus, cooking for 2-3 minutes. Then remove using a slotted spoon and transfer to a large mixing bowl.
Next, add the baby potatoes and cook them until fork-tender, approx. 15-20 minutes. Drain and rinse the potatoes until they are cool enough to handle.
While the potatoes are cooking, add the dressing ingredients to a small bowl or jar and mix well. If needed, add a few drops of water to thin the dressing.
Slice the cooked potatoes in half (or quarters if they are larger) and add them as well as the red onion to the bowl of peas and asparagus. Then add the dressing and stir until evenly coated.
hints: Taste the dressing for salt and pepper before tossing with the salad. Adjust if needed.
You may prepare this potato asparagus salad in advance and keep it refrigerated for 1-2 days before serving.

title: Spicy Crispy Tofu with Veggies
description: This spicy crispy tofu recipe is bold and delicious with golden tofu bites and vibrant veggies served over zucchini noodles.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "149 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "24 g", "proteinContent": "9 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "1229 mg", "fiberContent": "1 g", "sugarContent": "14 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 12 ounces (350 grams) extra firm tofu GMO-free if possible
1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce or Tamari for gluten-free
1 tablespoon hot sauce I like Frank's or sriracha
⅓ cup low-sodium soy sauce or Tamari for gluten-free
¼ cup cane sugar or sugar of choice
2 tablespoons hot sauce I like Frank's or sriracha
zucchini noodles, cauliflower rice, brown rice, quinoa, or barley
veggies of your choice I'm using broccoli and grape tomatoes
garnish with sesame seeds, chilves, green onion, cilantro and/or red pepper flakes
steps: Press the tofu

Cut your tofu into half-inch cubes. Then arrange some paper towels or a clean dish towel on a cutting board and place the tofu cubes in a single layer on top. Now add more paper towels on top of the cubes and place another cutting board, flat plate, or baking sheet on top. Finally, place something very heavy on top like a cast-iron skillet or a heavy book. Press like this for 15 minutes while you prepare the remaining ingredients.
For the tofu
Preheat the oven to 425°F/218°C convection bake and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
For the tofu
Add the pressed tofu cubes to a mixing bowl and gently toss with the soy sauce and hot sauce. Then add the onion powder and cornstarch and gently mix.
For the tofu

Arrange the coated tofu cubes in a single layer on your baking sheet, leaving space between each piece. Bake for 20-25 minutes, flipping once after 10 minutes.NOTE: If you do not have a convection oven, it may take a little longer to reach desired crispiness.
For the sauce
While the tofu is baking, combine all the sauce ingredients in a shallow pan, whisk until combined and simmer over medium-high heat until thickened, approximately 2-3 minutes.
For the sauce
Add the baked crispy tofu to the pan with the marinade and stir to coat.
For the sauce
Serve with grains, veggies, and garnishes of your choice.
hints: Arrange the cubes of tofu in a single layer with space between each piece . They shouldn't touch each other on the baking tray in order to get the maximum crisp level.
If you don't have a convection oven , it may take a few extra minutes for the tofu to get crispy. Bake until the desired crispiness level is reached.
For best texture , plan to enjoy this dish immediately. The longer it sits in the sauce, it will lose some of its crispy exterior.

title: Vegan Banana Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: These vegan banana chocolate chip cookies are chewy perfection and ready in no time!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "148 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "28 g", "proteinContent": "3 g", "fatContent": "4 g", "saturatedFatContent": "3 g", "sodiumContent": "137 mg", "fiberContent": "2 g", "sugarContent": "14 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: ¾ cup mashed banana approx. 2 bananas
⅓ cup cane sugar or coconut sugar
120 grams whole wheat flour approx. 1 cup spooned + levelled
steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mash the bananas in a mixing bowl and add the applesauce and sugar. Mix well.
Next, add all the dry ingredients: flour, baking soda, salt and stir until combined without overmixing. Then fold in the chocolate chips.

Scoop the mixture using a medium cookie scoop onto your prepared tray, leaving plenty of space between each cookie. You should get approx. 9 cookies. (Or use a small cookie scoop to get approx. 18 smaller cookies.)

Bake for 12-15 minutes or until the edges and bottoms are golden brown. Remove the cookies from the oven and let them cool at room temperature for at least 15 minutes before handling them and transferring to a cooling rack.
hints: Use very ripe bananas for the best flavour and natural sweetness. The skins should be spotted brown.
I recommend using a kitchen scale to weigh the flour for the best results. Scooping flour from a bag can often lead to too much flour being used, resulting in denser cookies.
Leave plenty of space between your cookie dough balls to allow the cookies to spread in the oven.
Leftover cookies will keep at room temperature for 2 days, in the fridge for 3-4 days, or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Asparagus and Tomato Pasta
description: This creamy asparagus and tomato pasta is the perfect balance of fresh, vibrant flavors and rich, indulgent comfort!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "290 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "56 g", "proteinContent": "12 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "85 mg", "fiberContent": "5 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 8 ounces (½ lb) pennette also known as penne piccole (or pasta of choice)
1 bunch asparagus ends trimmed and cut into 1.5-inch strips
2 cups cherry tomatoes or grape tomatoes
½ cup soy milk or non-dairy milk of choice
red pepper flakes, fresh basil or parsley
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta according to package directions for 'al dente' pasta. (Normally 2 minutes less than fully cooked.) Drain it, BUT reserve ½ cup or so of the pasta water, and set it aside in case it's needed later. Set the cooked pasta aside.
Meanwhile, add all the sauce ingredients to a bowl or measuring cup and whisk to combine. Set it aside.

Then, use a large skillet to sauté your garlic with 2-3 tablespoons of water or broth for approx. 60 seconds, stirring often. (You may use 1-2 tablespoons of olive oil if preferred, but note that this will increase the calories and fat.) Then add the tomatoes and asparagus to the skillet and stir occasionally for 2-3 minutes.
Add the whisked sauce to your pan with the veggies and simmer for 2-3 minutes until the sauce is thickened.
Toss in the cooked pasta and some reserved pasta water if you prefer a thinner sauce. Stir and serve with vegan parmesan cheese and/or red pepper flakes.

title: Asparagus Sheet Pan Dinner
description: This asparagus sheet pan dinner is a quick, easy, and flavourful meal that's perfect for busy weeknights.

ingredients: 1 bunch asparagus (ends trimmed and cut into 2-inch strips)
1 cup brown rice or quinoa (or grain of your choice)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection bake or roast if you have a roast setting, and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Combine all the marinade ingredients in a small bowl. Then add the prepared veggies and chickpeas to a large bowl and toss with the marinade. Arrange the veggies in a single layer on your baking sheet and roast for approximately 20-25 minutes, until golden brown.

Meanwhile, prepare your grain of choice. Cook the rice, quinoa, or grain of choice on the stovetop or in a rice cooker according to the package directions. (NOTE: Use broth instead of water to cook your grains for added flavour.)
Serve your cooked grains in bowls with the veggies and chickpeas on top.

title: Vegan Taco Salad
description: If you’re craving something fresh, satisfying, and full of flavour, this vegan taco salad is your answer!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "397 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "46 g", "proteinContent": "17 g", "fatContent": "21 g", "saturatedFatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "1201 mg", "fiberContent": "17 g", "sugarContent": "5 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "18 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 3 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce or tamari for gluten-free
15 ounce can black beans drained + rinsed
½ cup corn frozen and thawed or canned
jalapeno, avocado slices, fresh cilantro, tortilla chips or strips
steps: Add all the taco meat ingredients to your food processor and pulse until chopped, but still crumbly with lots of texture. Do not overprocess. Taste for salt and pepper, and add some if needed.
Transfer the "meat" to a large mixing bowl and add all the remaining salad ingredients to the same bowl. Mix well.

Choose a salad dressing from the options listed above, or anything else you'd prefer. If you plan to have leftovers, I recommend serving the dressing on each bowl, rather than mixing it into the salad, so you can store them separately to prevent sogginess.
hints: Do not overprocess the taco meat. You don’t want it blended, so pulse until crumbled and keep lots of texture for best results.
Store the salad and your dressing of your choice separately to keep the salad from getting soggy.

Leftovers will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days. The nutritional information includes the taco meat and the salad ingredients without the dressing or additional optional toppings. The nutritional information for the dressing will vary according to what you choose. You will find that nutritional information below each dressing recipe.

title: Beet Pasta Salad
description: This vibrant beet pasta salad combines tender beets with al dente pasta, tossed in a tangy vinaigrette.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "388 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "66 g", "proteinContent": "10 g", "fatContent": "10 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "149 mg", "fiberContent": "4 g", "sugarContent": "17 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "8 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: ½ pound rotini pasta or pasta of your choice

steps: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil and cook your pasta according to package directions for "al dente" pasta. Immediately drain and rinse the pasta to prevent overcooking. Then transfer it to a large bowl.
While the pasta is cooking, combine all the salad dressing ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.

hints: Salt your pasta water. Make sure to add enough salt to your pot of water for best texture and flavour. Here's a handy guide to help you salt your water perfectly each time.

Cook your pasta al dente. Do not overcook! Al dente means that the pasta is still firm once cooked, giving optimal texture in every bite. To ensure your pasta does not overcook, start taste testing a few minutes before the package says it will be ready. It should be tender, but still firm.
Leftovers will keep refrigerated for 3-4 days.

title: Cauliflower and Lentil Soup
description: This vegan cauliflower and lentil soup is a hearty, nutritious dish packed with flavour.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "103 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "20 g", "proteinContent": "7 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "318 mg", "fiberContent": "7 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 5 cups cauliflower florets cut into bite-size pieces
1 cup tomato sauce or tomato puree of choice
fresh parsley or basil finely chopped, for garnish
steps: In a large soup pot or dutch oven, sauté the onions and carrots with 1-2 tablespoons of water or broth until softened. Approx. 5-7 minutes. Then add the garlic and stir until fragrant, approx. 30 seconds.

Add all the remaining ingredients (except garnishes) to your pot and bring the soup to a boil. Then reduce to medium heat, cooking your soup with the lid on until the lentils and cauliflower are cooked, approx. 15-20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and remove the bay leaves and sprigs of rosemary from the pot. Taste for salt and pepper, and adjust if needed. Then serve.
hints: Use a very flavourful broth ! If your broth is lacking flavour, make sure to adjust the seasonings.
If you don't have any broth on hand , you can make some with this easy bouillon recipe . (I highly recommend this broth for its fantastic flavour.)
Depending on your preferred thickness , use 6-8 cups of vegetable broth. For a thicker soup, use six cups. For a thinner soup, use eight. Remember: the soup will absorb more liquid as it cools.
Leftovers keep refrigerated for up to 4 days. or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Beet Waffles
description: These vibrant vegan beet waffles are a deliciously unique twist on a breakfast classic.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "119 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "20 g", "proteinContent": "5 g", "fatContent": "3 g", "sodiumContent": "105 mg", "fiberContent": "3 g", "sugarContent": "1 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
steps: Combine the soy milk and apple cider vinegar in a large mixing bowl and set it aside for 5 minutes to thicken and curdle, creating your vegan buttermilk.
Preheat your waffle iron to medium/high heat, or according to the manufacturer's directions.
In a medium bowl, whisk together all the dry ingredients: flour, beet powder, baking powder.
By now, your soy milk should be curdled so add the applesauce and tahini to the bowl and stir. Then add the dry ingredients to the same bowl and stir until combined without overmixing.

Cook the waffles for 6-8 minutes, or according to the manufacturer's directions. Don't lift the lid too soon or the waffles may stick and break. Check carefully and if they appear to be sticking, cook an additional 1-2 minutes and check again.

title: Healthy Beet Muffins
description: These healthy beet muffins are a vibrant and nourishing snack, perfect for breakfast or dessert!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "199 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "20 g", "proteinContent": "6 g", "fatContent": "12 g", "sodiumContent": "212 mg", "fiberContent": "3 g", "sugarContent": "11 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 2 x 398 ml (2 x 14 ounce) canned beets drained (approx. 2.5 cups of cubed beets)
300 grams superfine blanched almond flour approx. 3 scant cups
⅓ cup vegan chocolate chips plus a few more for topping your muffins if you'd like
steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and line a muffin pan with parchment liners.
Add all the wet ingredients to a blender and process until completely smooth. Set aside.
Then whisk together the dry ingredients in a large bowl. Pour the pureed liquid ingredients into the same bowl as the flour and stir until combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips if using, and then divide the batter between your 12 muffin tins, filling almost to the top.
Bake the muffins for 28-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center of a muffin comes out clean and dry.
Remove the pan from the oven and let the muffins rest at room temperature for at least 20-30 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to completely set.
hints: Weigh your flour for the most accurate results . If you don't have a kitchen scale, spoon the flour into your measuring cup and use a knife to scrape off the excess, with similar results. Do not scoop from the bag!
If using canned beets , make sure they are not pickled! Use beets canned only in water, no vinegar or oil as that will alter the flavour.
Use fresh and active baking powder. Baking powder that is open in your pantry for 6+ months can lose its effectiveness.
Gently tap the muffin tray on a hard surface to close up any gaps in the batter before baking.
Let your muffins cool in the pan for at least 20-30 minutes before handling them. They are delicate and need time to completely set before transferring them to a wire rack.
Leftovers keep at room temperature for up to 2 days, in the fridge for up to 5 days, or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Chickpea Chocolate Spread [Nut-Free Nutella]

title: Roasted Beet Pasta Sauce
description: This vegan beet pasta sauce is a vibrant and creamy dish made with roasted beets, garlic, onion, and vegetable broth, blended to a smooth texture.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "367 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "65 g", "proteinContent": "14 g", "fatContent": "6 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "145 mg", "fiberContent": "7 g", "sugarContent": "11 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "4 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 3 cups cubed beets approx. 2 medium beets
4 cloves garlic leave the peels on!
1 tablespoon white wine vinegar or 2-3 tablespoons lemon juice
250 grams (½ pound) spaghetti or pasta of your choice
fresh chives, fresh basil, fresh thyme, fresh mint or herbs of your choice
lemon zest, red pepper flakes, olive oil
steps: Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection roast and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. (If you do not have a convection oven, allow more time for roasting.)

Peel and cube the beets into small half-inch pieces and arrange them in a single layer on your tray with the quartered onion and garlic cloves. Roast the veggies for 25-30 minutes, until golden brown and the beets are fork-tender.

Meanwhile, bring a large pot of generously salted water to boil and cook the pasta according to package directions for 'al dente' pasta. Drain it BUT reserve 1/2 cup or so of the pasta water, and set it aside. Return the drained pasta to the pot.

By now, your veggies should be ready, so add them to your blender with all the remaining sauce ingredients and process until smooth and creamy. If needed. add some of the reserved pasta water to thin out the sauce. Then pour the sauce into the pot with the pasta and stir until evenly coated.
Serve with garnishes of your choice.
hints: Salt your pasta water. Make sure to add enough salt to your pot of water for the best texture and flavour. Here's a handy guide to help you salt your water perfectly each time.

Cook your pasta al dente. Do not overcook! Al dente means that the pasta is still firm once cooked, giving optimal texture in every bite. To ensure your pasta does not overcook, start taste testing a few minutes before the package says it will be ready. It should be tender, but still firm.
Reserve some pasta water when draining the cooked pasta to thin your sauce if needed.
If you do not have a high-speed powerful blender , soak the cashews in hot water for 20 minutes first, then drain them and use as directed.

Leftovers will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days. I do not recommend putting pasta in the freezer as it alters its texture. However, if you’re making extra sauce, the sauce can be frozen in an airtight container for up to 3 months.

title: Double Chocolate Chickpea Cookies
description: These chocolate chickpea cookies are a deliciously healthy dessert with a rich, gooey chocolate flavour.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "57 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "6 g", "proteinContent": "2 g", "fatContent": "4 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "16 mg", "fiberContent": "2 g", "sugarContent": "2 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "2 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1.5 cups chickpeas cooked or canned, approx. 15-ounce can drained + rinsed

25 grams raw unsweetened cocoa powder approx. ¼ cup spooned + levelled

steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and line a large baking sheet or two smaller ones with parchment paper.
Add all the ingredients, except the chocolate chips to your food processor. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. Then add the chocolate chips and pulse a few times to mix them in.

Use a small cookie scoop to scoop the chickpea cookie dough onto your baking tray. You will get around 28 cookies. Then, press a few chocolate chips into the tops of each cookie if you'd like. Shape your cookies and gently press them down as they won't spread much in the oven.

Keep the cookies at room temperature for 2-3 days, refrigerated for 3-4 days or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Cauliflower Sweet Potato Soup
description: This creamy cauliflower sweet potato soup is a comforting, nutrient-packed dish perfect for cozy evenings.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "164 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "35 g", "proteinContent": "8 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "342 mg", "fiberContent": "9 g", "sugarContent": "9 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 6 cups cauliflower florets (from approx. 1 small head of cauliflower)

Serve garnished with roasted cauliflower pieces and chives.

title: Vegan Double Chocolate Chip Cookies

title: Vegan Matcha Cookies
description: Vegan matcha cookies are delicious, with an earthy, vibrant flavour and a soft and chewy texture.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "87 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "16 g", "proteinContent": "3 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "82 mg", "fiberContent": "1 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Add all the dry ingredients to a large mixing bowl and whisk until combined. Then add the wet ingredients and stir until no floury bits remain.

Scoop the cookie batter onto your baking sheet to make 12 cookies. Then bake in your preheated oven for 8-9 minutes. They will be very soft when fresh out of the oven but will firm up as they cool down.
hints: Weigh your flour for the best results . Scooping into a measuring cup can compact the flour and you may end up with more than needed.
Use active baking powder . Baking powder that's been open in the pantry for several months may lose its effectiveness.
These cookies keep for 1-2 days at room temperature, up to 4 days in the fridge or up to 3 months in the freezer.

title: Beetroot and Sweet Potato Salad
description: A beetroot and sweet potato salad is a vibrant, nutritious dish that combines the earthy sweetness of roasted beets with the creamy richness of sweet potatoes.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "356 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "56 g", "proteinContent": "10 g", "fatContent": "12 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "160 mg", "fiberContent": "9 g", "sugarContent": "16 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "9 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 3 cups cubed beets approx. 1 pound (cut into half-inch cubes)
3 cups cubed sweet potato approx. 1 pound (cut into half-inch cubes)
1.5 cups white cannellini beans approx. 15-ounce can, drained + rinsed
¼ cup dried cranberries or pomegranate
steps: Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection roast and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Arrange your peeled beet and sweet potato cubes in a single layer on your tray and sprinkle generously with salt and black pepper. Roast them for 20-25 minutes or until the edges are golden brown and the cubes are fork-tender.

Meanwhile, add your rice and vegetable broth to a small saucepot and bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat and simmer until it's cooked, and the liquid is mostly absorbed. Fluff it up with a fork and set it aside to cool slightly.
Add all the salad dressing ingredients to a small bowl and whisk to combine. Set aside.

When the roasted vegetables and rice are ready, add them, along with all the remaining salad ingredients to a mixing bowl. Then pour in the salad dressing and mix well until evenly coated. Taste for salt and pepper and adjust if needed.
hints: Cut the beet and sweet potato cubes as uniformly as possible for even cooking.
To save prep time , you may use pre-cubed sweet potatoes and beets.
If you don't have a convection oven , roast the vegetables a little longer, until they are fork-tender and the edges are golden brown.
Keep leftovers in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 3-4 days.

title: Carrot and Lentil Soup
description: Carrot and lentil soup is a comforting, hearty, nutritious, and easy-to-make dish.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "339 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "69 g", "proteinContent": "17 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "saturatedFatContent": "0.2 g", "sodiumContent": "482 mg", "fiberContent": "23 g", "sugarContent": "15 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "0.7 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 2 pounds carrots peeled + roughly chopped (approx. 6 large carrots)
1.5 pounds sweet potatoes peeled + roughly chopped (approx. 2 medium potatoes)
2-3 tablespoons lemon juice to taste, optional but recommended
fresh parsley, cilantro, coriander, freshly grated ginger, or a drizzle of olive oil
steps: Add the onion and garlic to a large pot with a tablespoon of water or broth (or oil if preferred) and sauté over medium heat until translucent, approx. 5 minutes.

Then add all the remaining ingredients except the lemon juice. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the lentils are cooked and the carrots and sweet potatoes are fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Turn off the heat and use an immersion blender to puree the soup. Then add the lemon juice, salt and pepper to your taste, and enjoy.
hints: Start with 8 cups of broth, but add more if you prefer a thinner soup.
As leftovers sit in the fridge, the soup will thicken. You may add more water or broth when reheating if you want to thin out the soup.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3-4 days or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Vegan Banana Pumpkin Bread
description: Indulge in the perfect autumn treat with this vegan pumpkin banana bread! Moist, flavorful, and easy to make!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "127 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "29 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "77 mg", "fiberContent": "4 g", "sugarContent": "9 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1 cup mashed banana from approx. 3 medium bananas
¼ cup soy milk or another plant-based milk
270 grams whole wheat all purpose flour approx. 2 cups
⅓ cup semi-sweet or dark chocolate chips plus more for topping
steps: Preheat your oven to 350℉/176℃ and line a loaf pan with parchment paper.
Mash the bananas and combine all the wet ingredients in a large bowl. Then add the dry ingredients and still until combined without overmixing. Fold in the chocolate chips if using.
Pour the batter into your lined loaf pan, smoothing out the top and adding more chocolate chips to the top if you'd like. Gently press them down.

Bake the pumpkin banana bread for 45-55 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. Then remove it from the oven and let rest for 15-20 minutes before transferring the loaf to a cooling rack or cutting board to continue cooling.
hints: Weigh the flour using a kitchen scale for the most accurate results . Scooping flour from a bag often results in too much flour being used and can alter the texture.
Use overly ripe bananas. The more brown spots, the better, as the sweeter they will be. Since the recipe uses very little sweetener, you want to make sure your bananas will provide ample sweetness.
Measure your mashed bananas. Bananas vary in size. So make sure to use enough for sweetness and moisture. Measure 1 full cup of mashed banana.
Use fresh + active baking powder ! Baking powder that has been open in the pantry for 6+ months may start to lose its effectiveness.

Use parchment paper to line your loaf pan. Although a nonstick loaf pan will do the trick, I find it easier to remove the loaf from the pan when using parchment paper. You can easily lift the bread out and place it on a wire rack without breaking it.
Individual ovens will vary. So test the doneness of your pumpkin banana bread using a toothpick inserted in the middle. When it comes out mostly dry and clean, it’s ready.
Let it cool. Allow extra time for the loaf cool down. A minimum of 20-30 mins on a cooling rack is recommended to completely set and make it easier to slice.
Leftovers keep at room temperature for 2-3 days, in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, or freeze it for up to 3 months.

title: Pumpkin Waffles
description: Indulge in the cozy flavours of fall with our vegan pumpkin waffles!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "128 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "26 g", "proteinContent": "5 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "100 mg", "fiberContent": "4 g", "sugarContent": "5 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1.25 cups soy milk (or non-dairy milk of choice)
steps: Preheat your waffle iron over medium heat.
Combine all the wet ingredients in a mixing bowl. Then add the dry ingredients and stir until combined without overmixing.
Ladle the waffle batter onto your preheated waffle iron and cook them for approx. 7-8 minutes. NOTE: These waffles take a little longer to cook than classic waffles.
Serve the waffles warm with chocolate chips, fresh fruit, nuts, maple syrup or any of your favourite toppings.

title: Roasted Beetroot Pumpkin Salad
description: Don't miss this vibrant and delicious roasted beetroot pumpkin salad.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "262 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "38 g", "proteinContent": "9 g", "fatContent": "10 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "257 mg", "fiberContent": "7 g", "sugarContent": "18 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "8 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 6 cups cubed pumpkin from approx. 2 pound pie pumpkin
3 cups cubed beets from approx. 1 pound of beets
15 ounce can chickpeas drained + rinsed, approx. 1.5 cups
steps: Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection roast. (If you don't have a convection oven, allow extra time to roast vegetables.) Line a large baking tray (or two smaller ones) with parchment paper and set aside.

Peel and cube your beets and pumpkin into half-inch pieces for quick cooking. Then arrange them in a single layer on your baking tray and sprinkle them with salt and pepper. Roast for 25 minutes. Then remove the tray from the oven, add the chickpeas and continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes until the veggies are fork tender and the chickpeas are crispy.
Meanwhile, combine the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.
Add the roasted vegetables, chickpeas, almonds, cranberries, and salad dressing to a large bowl. Stir until evenly coated, and serve warm or refrigerate for 1 hour before serving the salad.
hints: Chop the beets and pumpkin into small cubes for quicker cooking .
To save time , you may purchase cubed pumpkin pieces and beets from the store.
Taste and adjust the salad dressing, adding sea salt and black pepper to your taste before you toss it with the salad.
Leftovers will keep in the fridge for 2-3 days in an airtight container.

title: Peas + Mushroom Quinotto
description: Dive into the creamy goodness of quinotto, a unique and delicious twist on Italian risotto using quinoa for a wholesome boost.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "268 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "42 g", "proteinContent": "14 g", "fatContent": "4 g", "sodiumContent": "198 mg", "fiberContent": "8 g", "sugarContent": "7 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: ½ cup soy milk or non-dairy milk of choice
steps: Preheat a large skillet or cast iron pan. Then add the sliced mushrooms and sauté them until reduced. You should not need any oil as the mushrooms will release a lot of moisture as they cook.

Once reduced, add the garlic, stirring often for about 30 seconds. Then add the quinoa, stirring and toasting for another 30 seconds. Next, add the white wine, and stir constantly until mostly absorbed.

Gradually add the broth, approx. 1/2-3/4 cup at a time, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is mostly absorbed. Continue adding broth in this pattern. Once absorbed, add more until the quinoa is cooked through. This process will take around 15-20 minutes. (Don't dump all the broth into the quinotto at once.)
Then turn off the heat and stir in the peas, milk, and lemon juice. Taste for salt and pepper, and adjust to your taste. Depending on the saltiness of your broth, you may or may not need to add salt.
Serve your quinotto with vegan parmesan cheese and/or red pepper flakes.
hints: Use wine that tastes good ! If you won't drink it, don't cook with it either.
Do NOT add all the broth at once to your pan of quinotto. Add it slowly, as directed and add more only once mostly absorbed.
Leftovers keep refrigerated for 3-4 days. Reheat on the stovetop, adding a little water or broth to the pan to loosen up the quinotto as needed.

title: Salted Caramel Bliss Balls
description: Delicious salted caramel bliss balls are a fun bite-sized treat that's both satisfying and wholesome.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "77 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "7 g", "proteinContent": "1 g", "fatContent": "6 g", "sodiumContent": "33 mg", "fiberContent": "1 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1 cup macadamia nuts raw or dry roasted
¼ teaspoon sea salt reduce if using salted macadamia nuts
steps: Add all 4 ingredients to your food processor and process until combined and you have an even consistency, without overprocessing. (Some texture is nice.)
Scoop the batter and roll it into bite-sized balls, placing each one on a flat plate or baking sheet. You should get around 18 balls depending their size.
Optional: Roll some or all of the balls into dessicated coconut.
hints: If your dates are very dry , soak them in hot water for 10-15 minutes, and then drain them before adding them to your food processor. This will help soften them and make them easier to process.
Use raw macadamia nuts OR dry roasted, with or without salt. However, if the nuts are salted , halve the added salt.
Don't overprocess the mixture . These taste best with a little texture; process until combined without overdoing it.
These energy bites keep at room temperature for 2-3 days, in the fridge for up to 1 week or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Vegan Sweet Potato Mash
description: Indulge in the creamy goodness of our vegan sweet potato mash!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "250 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "59 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "sodiumContent": "708 mg", "fiberContent": "7 g", "sugarContent": "22 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 2 pounds sweet potatoes (choose narrow and long potatoes for quicker cooking)
1-2 teaspoons sea salt (or to your taste)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection roast. If your oven does not have a convection feature, bake your potatoes longer.

Line a baking sheet with parchment, pierce your potatoes several times with a fork and place them on the tray. Then roast your sweet potatoes for 35-55 minutes, until soft and easily pieced with a fork. The cook time will vary according to the size of your potatoes, and whether or not you're using a convection oven.

Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven and let them cool for 2-3 minutes. Then slice each one in half, pull the peel back, and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Add the maple syrup, cinnamon, and salt to the same bowl, and use a large fork or potato mashed to mash the potatoes and combine with the other ingredients.
Serve warm.

title: Vegan Blondies with White Beans
description: Rich and fudgy vegan blondies with a base of white beans! Delicious, sweet and wholesome!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "145 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "21 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "fatContent": "6 g", "sodiumContent": "22 mg", "fiberContent": "3 g", "sugarContent": "11 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1.25 cups white cannellini beans approx. 13.5 ounce can, drained + rinsed
100 grams blanched almond flour approx. 1 cup
¼ cup vegan chocolate chips optional, but recommended
steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and line a loaf pan with parchment paper. Set it aside.
Add everything except the chocolate chips to a food processor and blend until smooth and combined.
Transfer the blondie mixture to your loaf pan and smooth the top with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula. Then top with the chocolate chips if you're using them. Gently press them down.

Bake the vegan blondies in your preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean and dry. Then remove from the oven and let cool for 10-15 minutes in the pan before transferring to a wire rack to continue cooling. The blondies will be easier to slice once cooled.
hints: Use parchment paper to line your pan. Although greasing will do the trick for nonstick, it will be a lot easier to remove the brownies using the paper to lift them out. (And they'll cool faster this way!)
Wet your knife in between cuts when slicing your blondies, for smoother, nicer-looking edges and to prevent sticking.
The optional chocolate chips are INCLUDED in the nutritional information below.
Leftovers keep at room temperature for 2-3 days, up to 1 week in the fridge, or keep them frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Brown Rice and Quinoa Salad
description: A hearty, filling, delicious brown rice and quinoa salad with fresh veggies and a protein-packed creamy dressing.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "216 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "31 g", "proteinContent": "8 g", "fatContent": "7 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "13 mg", "fiberContent": "6 g", "sugarContent": "4 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1 cup cooked brown rice approx. ½ cup dry
1 cup cooked quinoa approx. ⅓ cup dry
½ cup red onion finely chopped
½ cup fresh basil finely chopped
steps: Start by cooking your rice and quinoa according to package directions if you don't already have some cooked. I like to cook mine in broth for added flavour or you may use cold water with salt. To cook the grains, use a 2 to 1 ratio of dry grains to liquid. Bring them to a boil, and then reduce the heat and simmer with the lid on until cooked through and the water is absorbed.
While the grains are cooking, prepare and chop all the veggies. Then, combine all the salad dressing ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.

Once the grains are cooked, fluff them with a fork and set aside to cool slightly before combining them with the remaining salad ingredients. Then toss everything with the dressing and refrigerate the salad for 1 hour before serving.

title: Vegan Banana Waffles
description: Indulge in the sweet, wholesome goodness of vegan banana waffles.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "118 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "25 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "126 mg", "fiberContent": "4 g", "sugarContent": "3 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1 cup mashed banana from approx. 2 large bananas

steps: Preheat your waffle maker over medium-high heat, or according to its manufacturer directions.

title: Apple Overnight Oats
description: Apple overnight oats make a quick, delicious, and wholesome breakfast.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "354 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "76 g", "proteinContent": "7 g", "fatContent": "5 g", "sodiumContent": "177 mg", "fiberContent": "9 g", "sugarContent": "16 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1 cup unsweetened non-dairy milk (I like soy, oat, or almond)
1 diced apple (like Honeycrisp or granny smith)
steps: Add all the ingredients in a medium bowl and mix well. Then divide the mixture into 2 jars or bowls and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.

title: Smoky Lentil Dip
description: A smoky and delicious lentil dip that's savoury and protein-packed.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "180 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "22 g", "proteinContent": "10 g", "fatContent": "6 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "123 mg", "fiberContent": "10 g", "sugarContent": "1 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "5 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: ⅔ cup split red lentils dried
steps: Rinse and sort your lentils to discard any rocks or debris. Then place them in a small saucepot with the vegetable broth. Bring it to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until cooked through, approx. 8 minutes.
Drain the lentils but reserve the cooking water in case needed to thin out the lentil dip.

Transfer the cooked lentils to your food processor and add all the remaining ingredients. Blend until completely combined, adding 1-2 tablespoons of the lentil water if needed for a thinner dip. (Keep in mind that the lentils will continue to absorb liquid and the dip will thicken as it sits.)
Taste for salt and pepper and add if needed. Then serve your dip warm or refrigerate it for 1 hour or longer before serving.
hints: Cook the lentils in vegetable broth , not water, for the best flavour. If you don’t have broth on hand, try making our delicious bouillon mix .
If you must use water, be sure to add extra seasoning, to taste.
If using canned lentils , increase the seasoning to make up for the loss of vegetable broth.
Store leftovers in the fridge in a sealed container for 3-4 days. Or freeze the dip in an airtight container for up to 3 months.

title: Blueberry Bliss Balls
description: Blueberry bliss balls combine the natural sweetness of blueberries and dates with the richness of nuts and a hint of vanilla for a quick energy boost or guilt-free dessert.

steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and set it aside.

title: Burrito Zoodles
description: Enjoy a healthy twist on a classic with burrito zoodles!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "149 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "28 g", "proteinContent": "9 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "473 mg", "fiberContent": "10 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 15 ounce can black beans drained + rinsed

steps: Start by spiralizing your zucchini into noodles if you're not using packaged zoodles from the store. title: Corn Salad

title: Vegan Raspberry Muffins [Oil Free]
description: These vegan raspberry muffins strike a perfect balance of sweetness and tartness, boasting incredible moisture and irresistible flavour!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "131 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "24 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "141 mg", "fiberContent": "3 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 2 teaspoons lemon juice or apple cider vinegar
1 tablespoon lemon zest from approx. 1 large lemon
270 grams oat flour approx. 3 cups spooned + leveled
½ cup unrefined coconut sugar or brown sugar
steps: Preheat the oven to 375℉/190℃ and grab a muffin tray to fit 12 muffins. If you don't have a nonstick pan use paper liners or grease the tins.
Combine the soy milk and lemon juice in a large bowl and set it aside for 5 minutes to thicken and curdle. (This makes vegan buttermilk.)
Then add the lemon zest and applesauce to the bowl of curdled milk and mix.
Next, add the flour, sugar, baking powder and soda. Mix until combined without overmixing. Then gently fold in the raspberries.

Divide the batter between your 12 muffin cups and bake for 20-22 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. Remove from the oven and let cool for at least 20 minutes before carefully transferring to a cooling rack. The muffins are delicate, so let them cool before transferring.

If using the optional glaze, mix the sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl Once the muffins are completely cooled, drizzle them with the glaze and let them sit for a few minutes so the sugar hardens, and enjoy.
hints: Weigh your flour using a kitchen scale for the most accurate results ! Scooping flour from a bag will compact the flour, and could mean too much flour is being used which could result in a denser muffin.
Use FRESH + ACTIVE baking powder . Baking powder that has been open in the pantry for 6+ months may lose its effectiveness.
Let your muffins cool in their pan for at least 20 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack. These muffins are delicate when warm so give them time to cool to prevent breaking them.
If using the optional glaze, ensure the muffins are completely cooled first and glaze them just before serving. Storing glazed muffins in a sealed container will cause the glaze to melt.
The muffins will keep in a sealed container at room temperature for 2-3 days, refrigerated for up to 1 week or frozen for up to 3 months. Inspired by my Lemon Blueberry Muffins .

title: Miso Pesto Pasta
description: Fresh and incredibly flavourful miso pesto pasta!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "131 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "8 g", "proteinContent": "6 g", "fatContent": "9 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "479 mg", "fiberContent": "2 g", "sugarContent": "1 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "7 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 1.5 cups fresh basil leaves gently packed

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook your pasta according to package directions for 'al dente' pasta. If there are no package directions for 'al dente' undercook the pasta by 1-2 minutes.

ingredients: 340 grams (12 ounce) block extra firm tofu choose organic tofu that's GMO-free if possible

steps: If working ahead, freeze your tofu and thaw it before pressing. If not, just press to remove as much excess moisture as possible for the best texture.

Prepare the tofu hot dogs

Prepare the tofu hot dogs

Add the pressed tofu and everything else except the flour to your food processor. Process until combined. Then add 4 tablespoons of flour and pulse until combined. Check the consistency of your mixture, you want it slightly softer than Play-Doh. If it's very soft/wet, add the remaining flour and pulse again.
Prepare the tofu hot dogs
Decide if you're making 4 jumbo dogs or 8 smaller weiners. (Photographed are jumbo dogs.) Then cut 4 or 8 square sheets of parchment paper and aluminum foil, accordingly.
Prepare the tofu hot dogs

Divide your dough into 4 or 8 portions and place each on a parchment paper square with the aluminum foil below it. If you want perfectly portioned tofu dogs, use a kitchen scale, otherwise eyeball it.
Prepare the tofu hot dogs

Use your hands to shape the dough into a hot dog/log shape, and then snugly wrap it in the parchment and foil, twisting the ends like a candy wrapper. Place each wrapped dog on your baking tray and bake.
Baking Instructions

For 4 jumbo dogs bake them for 40 minutes, then flip and continue baking another 30-40 minutes until firm to the touch.For 8 smaller tofu dogs bake for 30 minutes, then flip and continue baking for another 20-30 minutes until firm to the touch.Remove from the oven, unwrap and let them rest for 5 minutes before grilling or serving. Grilling Instructions (optional)

hints: There is no added salt since I’m using Tamari which I find salty enough. However, you may add salt to your taste if needed.

Store leftovers in a container or jar at room temperature for up to 5 days.

hints: Use overly ripe bananas with lots of brown spots on the peel for extra sweetness. You may also use frozen bananas, just let them come to room temperature before mashing them.
Don’t overmix . The texture of the muffins comes out best when folded together until just combined.
Let your muffins rest for 10 minutes after baking . This short cool-down time will allow your muffins to completely set, and prevent them from breaking when removing them from the pan.

If you don’t have oat flour on hand , you can make some by grinding oats in a high-speed blender. Weigh the oats first and then blend them. You may also use whole wheat flour if a gluten-free option is not needed.

Pumpkin pie spice works if you don’t have the individual spices. Use three teaspoons of the mix to replace the cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger.
For soy-free , use almond milk, cashew milk , or another non-dairy milk of your choice.
These banana pumpkin muffins will keep covered at room temperature for 2-3 days, or refrigerated for up to 4 days. Freeze the muffins airtight for up to 3 months.

title: Air Fryer Peas (Two Flavours)

title: Oil Free Vegan Cornbread

ingredients: 1 cup soy milk or plant milk of choice

title: Healthy Vegan Lemon Loaf
description: A wholesome and delicious vegan lemon loaf that's satisfying and easy to make!

hints: Use active baking powder . Oat and rice flour are denser than white flour and need a little extra to rise nicely. If your baking powder is very old or has been open in your pantry for 6+ months, it may start to lose its effectiveness. Test it before using it if you’re unsure.
If you don’t have a high-speed blender or your dates are very dry, soak them first for 15 minutes in hot water, and then drain them. This will soften the dates, making them easier to blend.
Don’t dump all the date syrup into the loaf. Make sure to follow the instructions carefully. Use only 1.5 cups of your syrup, and reserve the rest for the glaze.

The spices are subtle in flavour, since the lemon is the star of this dessert. For stronger spice , double the cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg called for in the recipe.
Cool your loaf to room temperature before glazing . Once glazed, let it rest for a few minutes so it slightly hardens before slicing.

title: Air Fryer Potatoes and Onions

title: Vegan Chicken Salad w/ Roasted Jackfruit

Leftovers will keep refrigerated in a sealed container for 2-3 days.

title: Vegan Waffle Potatoes
description: Crispy on the outside, fluffy in the middle, and incredibly delicious vegan waffle potatoes!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "135 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "31 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "sodiumContent": "9 mg", "fiberContent": "2 g", "sugarContent": "1 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder (to taste)
steps: Add the potatoes to a pot of generously salted water and bring it to a boil. Cook the potatoes until fork tender, approx. 10-15 minutes depending on the potato size.

Drain the water and transfer the potatoes to a cutting board, or another work surface. Once cool enough to handle, you may press the potatoes down using a potato masher, or the bottom of a cup, OR cut them in half lengthwise.

Cook them for 5-8 minutes, or until desired crispiness is reached. This will vary according to your waffle iron, and the size of your potatoes.
Serve them with green onions and dipping sauce of your choice.

title: Vegan Cajun Pasta
description: Spicy vegan Cajun pasta is a fantastic weeknight meal that's filled with flavour, fresh veggies, and chickpeas.

1 cup soy milk or other dairy-free milk

For the vegan Cajun pasta sauce
steps: Make sure to prep all your ingredients and chop your vegetables before you begin, since this dish moves along rather quickly.
Cook your penne in a pot of generously salted water, according to the package directions for 'al dente' pasta. Drain and set it aside.
Meanwhile, combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl or measuring cup, and set it aside.

Then, add the chopped onion, mushrooms, and peppers to a sauté pan with 1/4 cup of water. Sauté over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring often, until the veggies are tender, but do not overcook them. Then add the chickpeas and the sauce you just mixed in the previous step to the same pan. Mix well and let that simmer for 3-4 minutes to slightly thicken the sauce. Taste the sauce once cooked and add more Cajun seasoning if a spicier sauce is preferred, or add some salt and black pepper, if needed. (This will vary according to the broth you’ve used.)

I made this CAJUN SEASONING BLEND for this dish. Results and spice levels will vary according to the recipe or store-bought brand being used. Taste your blend to ensure the spice level is to your liking.
Keep leftovers in the fridge for 3-4 days.

title: Chickpea Asian Buddha Bowl
description: An Asian Buddha bowl that is absolutely BURSTING with flavour!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "396 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "67 g", "proteinContent": "19 g", "fatContent": "14 g", "saturatedFatContent": "3 g", "sodiumContent": "484 mg", "fiberContent": "15 g", "sugarContent": "14 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "10 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 4 cups cubed sweet potatoes cut into half-inch cubes (approx. 2 medium potatoes)
3 cups chickpeas cooked or canned (approx. 2 15-ounce cans)
4-5 bunches baby bok choy base stem removed and leaves separated
2 tablespoons lime juice approx. 1 medium lime
2 tablespoons low sodium soy sauce or Tamari for gluten-free
1 teaspoon freshly grated ginger approx. 1-inch knob
¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes or to taste
green onion, chives, scallions, sesame seeds
steps: Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection roast (or bake) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Arrange the sweet potato cubes in a single layer, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and roast them for 20 minutes, then flip and roast for another 10-15 minutes. Set aside.
Meanwhile, combine all the peanut sauce ingredients in a medium bowl and set aside.

Add the vegetable broth, 1 clove of minced garlic, and the red pepper flakes to a large pan and sauté for 30-60 seconds. Then add the bok choy and sauté on both sides for 1-2 minutes until wilted and coated with the garlic and spice. Transfer it to a plate and set aside.
To the same pan, add the peanut sauce and chickpeas, simmer for 2-3 minutes, and then turn off the heat.
Arrange the saucy chickpeas, bok choy, and sweet potatoes in bowls and serve with cooked rice or noodles if desired.

title: Vegan Frittata Muffins [Vegan Savoury Muffins]
description: These vegan frittata muffins AKA vegan savoury muffins are the ultimate alternative to traditional egg cups that will satisfy your taste buds and kickstart your day.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "98 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "17 g", "proteinContent": "7 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "250 mg", "fiberContent": "4 g", "sugarContent": "3 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: ¼ cup yellow onion finely chopped
½ cup diced red bell pepper approx. 1 small pepper
1 cup diced cremini or baby bella mushrooms approx. 4-5 mushrooms
¾ cup broccoli finely chopped, approx. 3-5 florets
300 grams chickpea or garbanzo flour approx. 2 cups
1 teaspoon sea salt or sub half with black salt AKA kala namak
¼ teaspoon black pepper optional, but recommended
steps: Preheat the oven to 400℉/204℃ and grab a nonstick muffin pan or grease if needed.
Place all the chopped veggies in a pan and sprinkle them with a little salt and pepper, if desired. Dry sauté, stirring often, until reduced and softened, approx. 5 minutes. Set aside.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, add the chickpea flour, nutritional yeast, seasonings, and baking powder, and whisk to combine. Then pour in the water and mix well.

Divide the sautéed veggies between your 12 muffin tins, about 1 heaping tablespoon per muffin. Then pour the chickpea batter on top to evenly distribute it between your 12 muffins. Use a spoon to gently stir each muffin, to evenly distribute the veggies and the batter. (DON'T SKIP MIXING.)
Bake for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. Remove from the oven and let cool for at least 10 minutes. Then carefully remove them from the pan.
hints: Stir the muffins BEFORE baking . This will ensure even distribution of the veggies. Also, make sure that some batter gets to the bottom of the tins so the muffins will be evenly shaped and prevent sticking.
Alternatively , you may pour a tablespoon of chickpea batter into the bottom of each muffin tin, followed by the veggies, and then pour the remaining batter on top.
Let the muffins rest at room temperature for at least 10 minutes before removing them from the pan. This cool-down period helps muffins set so that they don’t break when removing them.

If you’re avoiding oil and don’t want to grease your muffin pan, let your muffins cool a little longer before attempting to remove them. Then use a butter knife to gently glide around each muffin if they are a little stuck, and scoop them out.

Leftovers keep in a sealed container in your fridge for up to 5 days. Or freeze them for up to 3 months. Make sure to completely cool the vegan egg muffins before refrigerating or freezing. You may reheat the egg cups in the microwave or toaster oven, or enjoy them cold.

title: Baked Vegan Glazed Donuts
description: Sweet, moist, and incredibly delicious vegan glazed donuts that are baked (not fried!) for the ultimate treat.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "144 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "33 g", "proteinContent": "3 g", "fatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "77 mg", "fiberContent": "2 g", "sugarContent": "17 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 240 grams whole wheat pastry flour approx. 2 cups
½ cup soy milk or other non-dairy milk
1-2 tablespoons soy milk or other dairy-free milk
steps: Preheat the oven to 350℉/176℃ and grab enough donut pans to make 12 donuts. (I use 2 pans of 6 donuts each.)
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and cinnamon in a medium mixing bowl. Then add the wet ingredients and stir until combined.

Divide the donut batter between the 12 donut tins and bake for 12-15 minutes. The donuts are ready when they are firm to the touch, but give a little when gently pressed. Remove from the oven and let them cool before glazing.
While the donuts are cooling, prepare the glaze. Combine the sugar, lemon juice, and milk (starting with 1 tablespoon) in a small bowl. Add a little more milk if needed.
Once cooled, dip the tops of each donut into the glaze, and place them glaze side up on a wire rack to let the glaze set. Enjoy!
hints: Weigh your flour using a kitchen scale for the most accurate results . Scooping flour from a bag may result in too much flour being used and could alter the texture.
Use fresh and active baking powder . Once opened, baking powder begins to lose its effectiveness, so it’s best to consume your baking powder within 6 months.
Allow your donuts to cool for 10-15 minutes before attempting to remove them from the pan. If the donuts are too hot, you risk breaking them.
Once transferred to a wire rack, let them continue to cool to room temperature before glazing them .
The nutritional information above includes 1 donut, with the glaze.

description: Crispy, creamy, savoury, and flavour-filled vegan scalloped potatoes! They make a perfect side dish for brunch or dinner.

description: This spicy Szechuan tofu recipe is filled with flavour, protein-dense, and a perfectly well-balanced meal.

steps: Press the tofu

Cut your tofu into half-inch cubes. Then arrange some paper towels or a clean dish towel on a cutting board and place the cubes in a single layer on top. Now add another clean dish towel on top of the cubes and another cutting board, flat plate, or baking sheet on top. Finally, place something very heavy on top like a cast-iron skillet or heavy books. Prepare the tofu
Preheat the oven to 425℉/218℃ convection bake and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Prepare the tofu
Once the tofu is pressed, place the cubes in a medium bowl with the soy sauce and gently mix. Then add the cornstarch and gently stir to coat the pieces.
Prepare the tofu

Arrange the tofu in a single layer on your baking sheet, leaving space in between each cube. Bake for 15 minutes, then flip, and bake for an additional 15-20 minutes, or until desired crispiness is reached.
For the Szechuan sauce + veggies
While the tofu is baking, combine all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and whisk together. Set aside.
For the Szechuan sauce + veggies

Preheat a cast iron pan or wok on your stovetop, and then add the frozen veggies to stir fry for 2-3 minutes (don't overcook them, they taste best when still a little crisp). Then add the sauce and let it simmer for 2-3 minutes with the veggies to slightly thicken the sauce.
For the Szechuan sauce + veggies

For the Szechuan sauce + veggies
Serve with grains of your choice or spiralized vegetable noodles. Then top with green onion and sesame seeds if you'd like.
hints: Try and cut your tofu cubes as uniformly as possible for even cooking and crispiness.

For the best texture , plan to enjoy your Szechuan tofu immediately. The longer it sits in the sauce, it will begin to lose its crispy exterior.
Leftovers keep refrigerated in a sealed container for 3-4 days.

title: Vegan Creme Brulee [No Refined Sugar!]

nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "calories": "200 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "36 g", "proteinContent": "8 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "108 mg", "fiberContent": "0.1 g", "sugarContent": "29 g", "servingSize": "1 serving"}
ingredients: 12 ounce (340 grams) extra firm tofu drained, use GMO-free soy if possible

steps: Add all the ingredients for the custard base to your food processor and blend until completely combined and smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.

title: Vegan Chocolate Zucchini Bread [No Oil or Sugar]
description: This vegan chocolate zucchini bread tastes more like a cake, but without all the sugar! Dates sweeten this delicious treat while hiding any trace of veggies!
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "servingSize": "1 Slice", "calories": "116 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "23 g", "proteinContent": "4 g", "fatContent": "2 g", "sodiumContent": "161 mg", "fiberContent": "3 g", "sugarContent": "9 g"}

Salt your pasta water. Make sure to add enough salt to your pot of water for best texture and flavour. Here's a handy guide to help you salt your water perfectly each time.

Leftovers keep refrigerated in a sealed container for 3-4 days, just reheat on the stovetop to enjoy. You may freeze any extra sauce for up to 3 months but freshly cooked pasta tastes best, so I don’t recommend freezing pasta.

title: Vegan Lentil Meatballs [Oil Free+GF]

title: Healthy Nutella Recipe [Vegan+Oil Free]
description: Healthy nutella that's chocolatey, rich and delicious, but naturally sweetened for a nutritious alternative to store bought.
nutrients_raw: {"@type": "NutritionInformation", "servingSize": "2 Tablespoons", "calories": "100 kcal", "carbohydrateContent": "9 g", "proteinContent": "2 g", "fatContent": "7 g", "saturatedFatContent": "1 g", "sodiumContent": "42 mg", "fiberContent": "2 g", "sugarContent": "6 g", "unsaturatedFatContent": "6 g"}

steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Add the raw hazelnuts in a single layer and bake for 15 minutes.

Return hazelnut butter back to the processor, along with the remaining plant milk, cocoa powder, vanilla, and salt. Pulse several times until blended. You may add an additional 2-3 tablespoons of milk if a thinner consistency is desired.
Store your healthy Nutella in a clean glass jar at room temperature for up to 1 week.
hints: After roasting the hazelnuts, work quickly to remove the skins as they come off easiest when warm. Most of the skins will come off easily, but don’t worry if there are a few stubborn ones.

While both a food processor and blender work well , a high-speed blender, like a Vitamix will yield smoother results. But in exchange, it’s easier to transfer the Nutella from a food processor bowl.

I like the sweetness level of this Nutella as is. However, if you want a sweeter Nutella , you may add a liquid sweetener, to taste, such as maple syrup, date syrup, or agave at the end and pulse a few times to mix through.
Recipe yields approx. 2 cups of healthy Nutella. Store in a clean glass jar at room temperature for up to 1 week. Refrigerate for up to 3 weeks. The serving size is two tablespoons.
